statement_verbatim:
statement: >-
    Overlap producers and consumers through incremental artifact delivery only with an explicit streaming protocol.

statement: >-
    Follow declared flow router routes and user/system flow continuations without additional scheduling or speculative transformations. Reference is the default, not a mandated slow path.

statement: >-
    Initiate reversible likely-needed work early only when discarded work and cancellation cannot change accepted behavior.

statement: 'Nothing is authored before the operator confirms the locked decomposition.
  The Ratify gate is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary: only on ratification
  does atdd plan (the system, not the agent) invoke atdd author <kind> per locked
  unit.'

statement: 'An atdd plan decomposition needs no PRE-EXISTING issue or up-front ceremony,
  but it MUST be bound to a local ATDD issue record before Ratify: on Ratify, atdd plan
  binds the locked decomposition to a target issue (or mints one from the main job) and
  authors the plan as that issue''s PLANNED-phase substrate on its registered branch +
  worktree. The binding identity is the LOCAL manifest/State Store record (its slug; #945/#1168),
  not a GitHub issue number — GitHub is a downstream extension that syncs the number after
  install, so the iron rule (issue + branch + worktree per repo modification) holds even
  with no GitHub. The session removes the up-front ceremony, not the issue.'

statement: Ratify cannot lock a user/system-flow-bearing plan when required flow router sanity
  fails.

statement: Ratify names the rungs of the granularity ladder a decomposition did not
  descend, so an operator is told that a locked plan is not testable end to end rather
  than having to notice it.

statement: 'atdd plan runs a gated decomposition session: Intent -> Attach -> Compose
  -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify. The stages name what the OPERATOR is
  deciding, not what the tool is doing. Stages are gates not scripts (free dialogue
  within a stage; backtracking allowed); a stage advances only when its exit condition
  (proper state) holds. These are the SESSION stages, and they are a separate
  vocabulary from the DESIRED OUTCOME job steps owned by steps.convention — do not read the two
  as one system.'

statement: A hand-authored plan unit spec is validated against its artifact schema
  — well-formedness at Compose, completeness at Ratify — so the by-construction guarantee
  atdd author makes is kept at the one layer where the spec is written by hand.

statement: Every convention node (any *.convention.yaml carrying a rule_id, test fixtures excluded) must appear as a source_ref or target_ref of at least one edge in the relationship graph (src/atdd/coach/graph/relationships.yaml). A node referenced by no edge is an orphan and is refused — the graph must cover every node, not just have no dangling edges.

statement: 'A feature marked `kind: feedback-loop` must have at least one SMOKE acceptance
  whose acceptance block declares a close_the_loop: field carrying both consumer_reacted
  and drift_resolved.'

statement: Each JTBD step declares its primary architecture layer(s) and a canonical
  call sequence across presentation, application, domain, and integration, giving
  a routable mapping from step to architecture.

statement: Every job decomposes into an ordered sequence of nine JTBD steps — define,
  locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, resolve, conclude — each with
  a fixed purpose, guiding question, and expected outputs.

statement: Each JTBD step is recognized and phrased through a fixed set of slotted
  linguistic templates that bind the step's verb to its objects and constraints.

statement: Steps are ordered and numbered, and each declares its pre-conditions and
  its outputs.

statement: A subject is a durable noun object registered in plan/_subjects.yaml before
  any user/system flow is typed under it; subjects are unique-by-subject and typed user/system flows are
  unique-by-subject+slug.

statement: >-
  Every acceptance declares telemetry with disposition required (naming at least one concrete
  telemetry URN that resolves to a tracking-plan entry) or disposition not-applicable (with a
  rationale), and every tracking-plan item's acceptance references resolve to declared acceptances
  (REQUIRED).
